experience:
Experience: Step 1: The robot did not manipulate any object and continued observing the current scene. The step succeeded, and the task was completed.

Key lesson learned: If the instruction is only to observe, the robot should perform no physical interaction at all. In similar cluttered tabletop scenes, it should sequence actions as follows: (1) read and classify the task as observation-only or manipulation, (2) keep the arm and gripper in a safe non-contact state, (3) inspect the scene visually and note object locations and relationships, and (4) end the task once the observation requirement is met. This strategy avoids unnecessary failures from accidental contact or unintended manipulation.

experience:
Experience: Step 1: The robot did not manipulate any object and continued observing the scene visually while keeping the gripper in a safe non-contact state. This step succeeded, and the task was completed.

Key lesson learned: If the instruction is only to observe the environment, the robot should not attempt to grasp, push, or reposition anything. In similar cluttered tabletop scenes, especially when objects are close to the gripper or include wires, small loose items, or partially visible devices, the robot should: 1) confirm that the task is observation-only, 2) avoid all contact, 3) keep the gripper and arm in a safe stationary pose with adequate clearance, 4) use vision to monitor the scene, and 5) end the task once observation is complete. This sequencing helps complete the task reliably without failure.
